decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Jamie points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Jamie keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Jamie a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Who said that?
decisions.situation: Your voice echoes in a stairwell. Whoever lives in the walls knows the same words as you, but always says them late.

choices.label: Try a very long hello
Try a quiet little word
Wait for the walls to start

result.title: A late reply
result.body: The walls return most of your hello. You start again before they finish.

journal.text: I discovered an echo and gave it a very long greeting.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Jamie asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Show Jamie your disappearing treasure
Try the other sock
Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Jamie supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Jamie the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Heavy traffic
decisions.situation: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.

choices.label: Crouch down and watch
Give it plenty of room
Challenge it to a race

result.title: Eventually, the other side
result.body: It reaches the edge and disappears under a leaf. You remain impressed by all the feet.

journal.text: I watched a caterpillar cross a path.

decisions.title: They do not find it funny
decisions.situation: Someone keeps making a joke out of Charlie’s name. Charlie has stopped correcting them.

choices.label: Use their name properly and speak up
Check on Charlie privately
Join in for a laugh

result.title: A little backup
result.body: You say it is getting old. Charlie thanks you later.

journal.text: I backed Charlie when someone kept mocking their name.

decisions.title: Hostile snack takeover
decisions.situation: Charlie offers a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They call the cracker “rare”. There are twelve more in the packet.

choices.label: Demand two snacks for your one
Eat your snack during the sales pitch
Split yours and spare the cracker

result.title: The negotiator gets greedy
result.body: Charlie nearly agrees, then notices you smiling. They withdraw the cracker and their goodwill.

journal.text: I tried to turn Charlie’s snack offer into a better deal for myself.

decisions.title: Nobody told the spy
decisions.situation: You catch Charlie explaining your secret code to everyone. They claim it is fine because they have invented a second, more secret code. You have not been told it.

choices.label: Demand to inspect the new codebook
Invent a silent signal for “you are fired”
Tell everyone the first code means nothing

result.title: One unhelpful entry
result.body: The new codebook contains one word: “banana”. Charlie says its meaning is classified. You add a second word meaning “tell your partner things”.

journal.text: I inspected Charlie’s replacement secret code and found one word.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Charlie is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Help interview the invisible applicants
Apply, despite being inconveniently real
Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Charlie rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Charlie interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: A complaint from past you
decisions.situation: You find a childhood letter addressed to yourself. It says, “If you are not a dinosaur by thirteen, you have ruined everything.” There is a drawing of the expected dinosaur.

choices.label: Make a tail out of socks and deliver a roar
Write a formal rejection on the back
Destroy the evidence

result.title: Partial compliance
result.body: The tail falls off during your first turn. You add “technical difficulties” beneath the original demand and draw yourself with better knees.

journal.text: I answered a childhood demand to become a dinosaur by making a sock tail.

decisions.title: Your name on the cover
decisions.situation: Charlie asks you to share a class project. Camille has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.

choices.label: Promise to write your section
Ask to work separately
Admit you cannot commit

result.title: Future You has been notified
result.body: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

journal.text: I agreed to write a section of a class project with Charlie.

decisions.title: The project is due
decisions.situation: Charlie is putting the class project together. Camille wants your section today. The blank page has enjoyed two months of peace.

choices.label: Finish your section
Ask Camille for help
Leave your section blank

result.title: Your name belongs on it
result.body: You finish your section and explain it to Charlie. Camille records the work you actually did.

journal.text: I finished my section of the class project with Charlie.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs CA$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Camille afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: A promise remembered
decisions.situation: Two years after that class project, Charlie Martin brings it up. Back then, you finished your section.

choices.label: Remember doing your part
Tell Charlie it does not matter
Leave it in the past

result.title: An old project, an honest conversation
result.body: You acknowledge that you finished your section. Charlie hears you out.

journal.text: I talked honestly with Charlie about our old project, when I finished my section.

decisions.title: The pancake is on the ceiling
decisions.situation: You help Jamie make “foolproof” pancakes. The first one is stuck to the ceiling. Neither of you wants to discuss how it got there.

choices.label: Consult the recipe before pancake two
Ask Jamie to demonstrate
Attempt the exact same toss again

result.title: The pan is a serving suggestion
result.body: The instructions recommend turning it gently. You complete the next batch without adding anything else to the ceiling.

journal.text: I read the recipe after a disastrous pancake toss with Jamie.

decisions.title: Sent to the group
decisions.situation: You send “Whoever made this group is unbearable” to the group itself. The admin replies, “Hi.” You can see several people typing.

choices.label: Mute the group and disappear
Admit you meant a different chat
Explain that autocorrect meant “adorable”

result.title: A successful retreat
result.body: You miss the replies and spend the afternoon doing something else. The message remains embarrassing; you stop watching it happen.

journal.text: I muted a group after sending an insulting message to it.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Jamie sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Jamie remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Jamie also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Toronto needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Toronto.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs CA$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Donate CA$350.14 to the donkey charity
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

List what you did achieve
Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.
